articles.title: India's Market Engine Has Quietly Switched Drivers — From Foreign Money to the Monthly SIP
articles.excerpt: Even as foreign investors pulled roughly $36 billion out of Indian equities and the Nifty went almost nowhere for two years, ordinary savers kept feeding the market through automated monthly plans — a shift JP Morgan calls the country's new 'demand anchor.'
articles.image_caption: Mumbai's financial district, where domestic monthly investment plans have become the dominant force in Indian equities
articles.nri_angle: NRIs weighing whether to keep money in Indian equities should understand that the market is now propped up less by the foreign flows they watch in the headlines and more by a domestic savings wave — a structural change that affects both the risks and the resilience of any India allocation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Quietly Talking Itself Out of Gold — and the World's Bullion Market Is Feeling It
articles.excerpt: Domestic gold has slid to its lowest price since early April, dealers are quoting steep discounts, and the country's gold ETFs just logged their first monthly outflow in a year. Behind the cooling is a deliberate push to curb gold buying and defend a battered rupee.
articles.image_caption: Indian gold demand has cooled to multi-month lows as the country curbs buying to defend the rupee
articles.nri_angle: Gold is woven into diaspora life — the wedding jewellery, the festival purchases, the rupee-denominated savings that NRIs hold as a hedge — so India’s campaign to cool gold demand, the slide in domestic prices and the steep dealer discounts directly shape when and how non-resident Indians buy, gift and store the metal both abroad and back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Markets Roar Back as Oil Crashes and the Central Bank Calms Rate Fears
articles.excerpt: A day after a brutal selloff, the Sensex jumped nearly 800 points and the Nifty reclaimed 24,000, powered by banks and IT, as Brent crude tumbled to four-month lows on signs the Strait of Hormuz was reopening and the RBI signalled no rate hike is coming.
articles.image_caption: The Sensex rallied nearly 800 points on June 24 as oil prices fell and the RBI eased rate-hike fears
articles.nri_angle: The same falling oil price and steadier rupee that lifted Mumbai’s indices directly shape what NRIs see — the value of remittances sent home, the returns on Indian equity and bond holdings, and the cost of the fuel and imports that drive India’s inflation — and a fresh RBI rule now lets banks lend to non-resident Indians against their foreign-currency deposits.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Threw Open Its Bond Market to the World. The World Is Still Deciding Whether to Walk In.
articles.excerpt: After scrapping the tax on foreign holdings of government bonds and widening access, India has lured early buyers — including a rare $1 billion bet by Canada's Fairfax — and is angling for a coveted Bloomberg index seat. But a weak rupee and steep hedging costs may yet keep the big money cautious.
articles.image_caption: India's bond-market reforms aim to lure global investors as a weak rupee tests their appetite
articles.nri_angle: India's push to pull global money into its government bonds runs on the same engine the diaspora is being courted with — dollar deposits, GIFT City, index inclusion — and the outcome will shape the yields, the rupee and the investment options NRIs see when they decide how much of their savings to send home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Opens a New Door to the World's Markets — and It Runs Through GIFT City
articles.excerpt: A wave of new funds is letting Indians invest in US stocks and global assets through the country's tax-neutral financial hub, with the fund itself shouldering the tax — but the fine print on remittance limits and levies still rewards a careful reading.
articles.image_caption: An Indian financial-district skyline; new funds based in GIFT City are opening fresh routes for Indians and NRIs to invest in global markets
articles.nri_angle: GIFT City is being built explicitly to court the diaspora's capital, and for NRIs weighing how to hold global assets with an Indian foot, the new IFSC funds change the calculus on tax, repatriation and paperwork — exactly the friction points that have long made cross-border investing a headache.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jio Files for India's Biggest-Ever IPO — but This Time, the Marquee Backers Don't Get to Cash Out
articles.excerpt: Reliance's digital arm has filed papers for a roughly $3.8 billion listing, with every rupee earmarked for debt and growth — meaning the Meta, Google and Gulf investors who poured in during 2020 will have to wait their turn.
articles.image_caption: Reliance Jio's headquarters. Jio Platforms has filed a draft prospectus for what would be India's largest-ever IPO.
articles.nri_angle: Jio's listing will be the marquee Indian IPO of a generation, and NRIs — long among the most eager retail buyers of marquee Indian names — will be weighing whether to chase it; the unusual all-fresh-issue structure and the holding-company discount are exactly the fine print diaspora investors need to read before committing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Wants to Grow at 10%. First It Has to Explain Why Foreign Investment Has Dried Up.
articles.excerpt: Net foreign direct investment fell to just $7.7 billion last year — a fraction of Vietnam's and Indonesia's — and India's top industry lobby says slow courts and five-year arbitration waits are scaring off the capital the country needs.
articles.image_caption: India's financial capital, Mumbai, where weak foreign direct investment is testing the country's growth ambitions
articles.nri_angle: NRIs are among the most natural foreign investors in India — through direct stakes, startups and property — yet the same slow courts and tangled dispute resolution that deter global capital are exactly what burn diaspora investors who get stuck in years-long litigation back home, making this a story about whether India can finally be trusted with their money.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tata Motors Bets on a Five-Year Turnaround — ₹6 Lakh Crore in Revenue, and a Promise to Clear Its Debt
articles.excerpt: At its investor day, Tata Motors' passenger-vehicle group set out targets to lift consolidated revenue past ₹6 lakh crore and reach a 10% margin by FY31, and to be net debt-free by FY29 — even as a cautious JLR outlook for FY27 left brokerages split.
articles.image_caption: Tata Motors' Jaguar Land Rover unit, maker of the Range Rover, anchors the group's five-year turnaround plan
articles.nri_angle: Tata Motors is both a heavyweight in the Nifty and Sensex that anchor most NRI India portfolios and the owner of Jaguar Land Rover, whose Range Rovers and Defenders the diaspora actually buys on the streets of London, New Jersey and Toronto — making its five-year bet a rare stock where the diaspora is invested in the shares and the showroom at once.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India’s Economy Just Cooled to a Three-Month Low — and a Resurgent Dollar Is Squeezing the Rupee Again
articles.excerpt: Fresh data show India’s private-sector growth slowing and business confidence at its weakest in nearly four years, just as rising bets on a U.S. Federal Reserve rate hike push the dollar to a one-year high and drag the rupee and Indian stocks lower.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai; Indian markets pulled back as growth cooled and a stronger dollar pressured the rupee
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs, the twin pressures matter directly: a weaker rupee stretches the value of dollars sent home or invested in India, while a cooling economy and a hawkish Fed reshape the calculus on when to remit, when to buy Indian equities, and how much currency risk to carry.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Courting the Diaspora’s Dollars to Rescue the Rupee — and Banks Are Racing to Cash In
articles.excerpt: The RBI is subsidising hedging costs on foreign-currency deposits and now letting domestic banks lend against them, in a 2013-style push to pull tens of billions of NRI dollars into the country. Analysts estimate the scheme could draw anywhere from $55 billion to $100 billion.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India is courting diaspora dollars through high-yield foreign-currency deposits to defend the rupee
articles.nri_angle: This scheme is aimed squarely at NRIs: with banks now offering 6–7 percent on dollar deposits — and leveraged structures that could push returns toward 12–15 percent — overseas Indians can earn high rupee-equivalent yields without taking on currency risk, while helping defend the very rupee their families back home depend on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Reliance Lays Out a Five-Year Plan to Double Its Earnings — With AI and the Sun at the Centre
articles.excerpt: At its 49th AGM, Mukesh Ambani's conglomerate paired a record-profit year with bold targets: doubling consolidated EBITDA, a ₹1-trillion FMCG business, an AI push across every product, and 200,000 green-energy jobs — even as the stock trades well below its peak.
articles.image_caption: Mukesh Ambani used Reliance's 49th AGM to set a five-year target of doubling the conglomerate's core earnings
articles.nri_angle: Reliance is the single heaviest weight in the Sensex and Nifty that anchor most NRI India portfolios and mutual-fund SIPs, so its five-year bet on AI, consumer brands and solar energy is, in effect, a bet on the direction of the entire market the diaspora invests in — and a preview of where India's economy is trying to go.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Bought More Russian Oil Than Ever — Right as Washington's Sanctions Waiver Expires
articles.excerpt: After the Iran war scrambled global energy flows, Russia's share of India's crude imports has nearly doubled to almost half, hitting a record 2.55 million barrels a day in June — but a lapsed US waiver now forces a tricky choice on Delhi's refiners.
articles.image_caption: Russia now supplies almost half of India's crude imports, with a record 2.55 million barrels a day arriving in June
articles.nri_angle: India's energy bill is the hidden hinge of its economy — it shapes inflation, the rupee NRIs send money in, and the stock indices the diaspora invests in — so how Delhi balances cheap Russian crude against renewed US sanctions pressure will ripple straight through the remittances and portfolios that tie the diaspora to home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Accenture Warning Knocks Indian IT — and the Bigger Fear Is What It Signals for Next Year
articles.excerpt: After the world's largest IT services firm trimmed its revenue outlook, Indian software giants like Infosys, TCS and Wipro slid as much as 7 percent, and brokerages warned that the coming financial year could prove tougher than the market has been pricing in.
articles.image_caption: Indian IT majors slid sharply after Accenture trimmed its revenue guidance, dragging the Nifty IT index lower
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT is the diaspora's bellwether industry — it employs many NRIs' relatives, anchors the portfolios of those who invest back home, and underpins the H-1B pipeline that brought a generation to America — so a warning that demand and AI are squeezing the sector touches NRI jobs, savings and family fortunes at once.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Faces Its Weakest Monsoon in 11 Years — but This Time the Economy Is Better Armoured
articles.excerpt: A strengthening El Niño has delayed the rains and brought dangerous heat, threatening harvests, food prices and growth. Yet bigger reservoirs and far wider irrigation mean the damage may be more contained than the alarming headlines suggest.
articles.image_caption: India faces its weakest monsoon in 11 years as a strengthening El Niño delays the rains and brings dangerous heat
articles.nri_angle: A poor monsoon feeds straight into the things NRIs watch most closely about India — food inflation that erodes the rupee's value, the central bank's room to cut rates, and the strength of the currency their remittances and investments are denominated in — making this year's rains a quiet but real input into diaspora financial decisions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gold Was Supposed to Soar During the Iran War. It Fell Nearly 10% Instead — Now JP Morgan Sees a 40% Rebound
articles.excerpt: The metal that diaspora families trust as a crisis hedge defied its safe-haven reputation, sliding even as conflict raged, before steadying near ₹1.46 lakh per 10 grams. The episode is a sharp lesson in how gold really behaves — and why timing it is a fool's errand.
articles.image_caption: Gold fell nearly 10% in India during the Iran war despite its safe-haven reputation, before steadying near ₹1.46 lakh per 10 grams
articles.nri_angle: Gold is the diaspora's instinctive store of value — bought for weddings, gifted at festivals, hoarded as insurance against bad times — so its counter-intuitive slide during an actual war, and the debate over where it goes next, speaks directly to how NRIs should size and time their single most emotional investment.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Burned Through Nearly $9 Billion in a Single Month Defending the Rupee — and Reserves Are at a One-Year Low
articles.excerpt: Fresh central bank data show the Reserve Bank of India sold a net $8.9 billion in April to slow the rupee's slide, capping a record fiscal year of intervention as foreign reserves fell to $671.6 billion and the currency clawed back from an all-time low.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India sold a net $8.9 billion in April to defend the rupee, with forex reserves falling to a one-year low
articles.nri_angle: The scale of the RBI's dollar-selling tells NRIs how hard their central bank is working to keep the rupee from sliding further — a direct signal on the value of remittances, NRE and FCNR deposits, and India-bound investments, and on whether the recent record lows are a floor or a way station.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Rupee Just Had Its Best Week in Months. Now a Resurgent Dollar Will Test Whether It Holds.
articles.excerpt: A drop in oil after the US-Iran peace deal pushed the rupee to 94.32, its strongest weekly run in 11 weeks — but a dollar at a one-year high and a hawkish Federal Reserve are pulling the currency back, while government bonds wait on the pace of foreign money returning.
articles.image_caption: The rupee posted its best week in months as oil prices fell, before a resurgent dollar tested the gains
articles.nri_angle: Every move in the rupee reprices the remittances NRIs send home, the value of their NRE and FCNR deposits, and the returns on their Indian investments — so a week that swung from oil-driven relief to dollar-driven pressure is not abstract macro news for the diaspora but a direct signal on when to send money and what their India holdings are worth.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
